why: Calls reached through a variable rather than a name — an annotated parameter, a chained call on a return value, and a class fetched from a lookup table. These are the shapes the extractors document as skipped, and this case exists to put a number on how much is lost.

known_gaps.why: `handler.run(payload)` on an annotated parameter. Resolving it needs type inference; the front-ends document this skip deliberately (typescript_extractor.py:20 states the equivalent for TS). Counted as a recall miss, not exempted.
`build(name).run(payload)` — a method call on the return value of another call. Needs the return type of `build`. Counted as a recall miss, not exempted.

`cls()` where `cls` came from a lookup table — construction through a variable. FOUND BY MEASUREMENT, NOT PREDICTED: the first scoring run emitted `build -> py:cls` instead. Recorded here after the fact and labelled as such, per the corpus rule that a gap noticed after seeing output is weaker evidence than one predicted before.

false_positives.why: `cls` is a LOCAL VARIABLE. The graph asserts a function named `cls` exists outside the scanned tree and that `build` calls it; both are false. This is invention, not incompleteness — the case exists partly to hold this defect visible. It costs CALLS precision (0.9 on this case) and should stay costing it until the extractor stops emitting it.

excluded: Module-level constants (svc.registry.TABLE) — DECIDED 2026-08-12: not a Field. A Field belongs to a Type in this vocabulary; module constants are not modelled, so labelling them would be a category error rather than a recall miss.
Calls to builtins (str) — the graph emits no node or edge for them at all, so there is no id to label.
